prompt:
You are an experienced sommelier comparing two wine recommenders. A
customer with no wine knowledge made this request:

"Can you help me pick a light, sweet wine for dessert to give my boss, just something safe that cannot go wrong?"

List A:
Wine 1: Muscat, US, $13. Tasting note: "This has a sweet charm to it, with a rich lemon flavor. This would be fine as a light dessert wine with lemon cake."
Wine 2: Sémillon, US, $48. Tasting note: "A very good dessert wine, whose acidity provides balance to the sweet apricot, orange, vanilla and honeysuckle flavors. A bit of tease, it would score far higher with greater intensity."
Wine 3: Black Muscat, US, $18. Tasting note: "A plummy, semi-sweet dark red wine that could stand a bit of a chill in the fridge. It has a nice chocolatey edge that would be a good partner with dark chocolate desserts. Finishes clean and with good acidity."
Wine 4: Moscato, US, $12. Tasting note: "Flowery and sweet through and through, this lighthearted dessert wine could also serve as apéritif as it's perfectly sippable, or as a pairing with something packed with spice, like enchiladas or red curry."
Wine 5: Muscat Canelli, US, $38. Tasting note: "This dessert wine is very sweet but not incredibly so, with a flavor like apricot and tangerine jam, drizzled with honey and vanilla extract and sprinkled with cinnamon. If that sounds delicious, it is, and the acidity makes it clean and zesty. The price isn't bad, considering that this is a full bottle, not a half bottle as so many dessert wines are."

List B:
Wine 1: Sémillon, US, $48. Tasting note: "A very good dessert wine, whose acidity provides balance to the sweet apricot, orange, vanilla and honeysuckle flavors. A bit of tease, it would score far higher with greater intensity."
Wine 2: Zinfandel, US, $20. Tasting note: "Other than being very sweet, this dessert wine has little to recommend it. It's soft and rich in white sugar flavors, with traces of oranges, red currants, chocolate and anise. High alcohol gives it a peppery burn."
Wine 3: Pinot Noir, France, $16. Tasting note: "A light and fruity wine with attractive red fruits and acidity. There is just a touch of tannin to hold the friendly fruitiness together."
Wine 4: Black Muscat, US, $18. Tasting note: "A plummy, semi-sweet dark red wine that could stand a bit of a chill in the fridge. It has a nice chocolatey edge that would be a good partner with dark chocolate desserts. Finishes clean and with good acidity."
Wine 5: Portuguese Red, Portugal, $7. Tasting note: "A soft, open wine with only light tannins. The fruit is just as light, with strawberry and some spice. For drinking now."

Which list answers the request better as a whole: relevance to every wish,
variety where the request leaves room, and fit for any occasion? If they
are equally good, say tie. Think briefly, then answer with JSON only:
{"reason": "<two sentences at most>", "better": "A" | "B" | "tie"}
